findings.case_fact: The amount and frequency of the beneficiary’s skilled care at the SNF decreased after August 11, 2009.

reason: The record shows daily intensive therapy, measurable functional improvement, and medical needs (IV pain medication, Coumadin adjustments, a possible effusion) that support an IRF-level stay, and the IME agreed. The passages do not settle whether a rehabilitation physician visited at least 3 days per week, or whether the reopening was timely, so those points are UNKNOWN.

findings.claim: Therapy intensity is shown by daily intensive therapy; the exact hours are not stated in the facts, so the 3-hours-per-day standard is not confirmed.
findings.quote: intensive therapies at least 3 hours per day at least 5 days per week
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary received intensive physical and occupational therapy each day after admission until discharge.

findings.claim: The beneficiary made measurable, practical functional improvement, which supports the expectation of significant benefit from the IRF program.
findings.quote: can reasonably be expected to make measurable improvement
findings.case_fact: ambulate 250 feet modified independent with front wheeled walker

findings.claim: Close physician involvement is partly supported by multiple physicians seeing the beneficiary. Whether a rehabilitation physician made the required face-to-face visits is UNKNOWN.
findings.quote: documented face-to-face visits from a rehabilitation physician at least 3 days per week
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary was seen at the IRF by at least three physicians and was monitored daily by the nursing staff.
